children: says that oil prices could climb as high as $120 a barrel if attacks on Middle East shipping escalate, as per Bloomberg report.
This favors positions in natural gas and diesel to benefit from potential gains,
Daan Struyven, co-head of global commodities research, said recent developments indicate a meaningful risk that shipping disruptions could expand and intensify.
Crude has risen to its highest level since July as the U.S. and Iran remain locked in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz.

The conflict, now more than six months old, has lifted a broad range of energy prices, with natural gas and petroleum products outperforming crude. Industrial fuel diesel has more than doubled this year.
Brent was last trading near $92 at the time of writing this report.

While Goldman sees significant upside for crude, Struyven said investors should hedge geopolitical risks by going long on global natural gas and refined-oil products, as supply disruptions are larger in those markets than in crude.
Goldman Sachs also sees oil falling to $80 a barrel if regional exports return to normal, Struyven said.

title: Goldman Sachs Flags $120 Oil Risk As Middle East Attacks Intensify
